key_insight: RASO uses a large external corpus of existing skills to initialize and iteratively improve a target skill, rather than relying only on costly agent rollouts.
engineering_relevance: This makes skill optimization more data-efficient and transferable across different tasks and harnesses, which is useful for building scalable agent systems.
method: RASI retrieves relevant skills and builds a knowledge-grounded initial prompt/skill without rollouts.
RASU uses execution feedback to retrieve additional external knowledge and refine the skill over time.
Cross-Harness Adaptation adjusts retrieved knowledge for both domain differences and harness mismatches.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on four agent benchmarks and two models, and the abstract reports consistent improvements over baselines without retrieval-augmented initialization or updating.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality, coverage, and harness compatibility of the external skill corpus, which could limit gains in sparse or highly specialized settings.
paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Skill Optimization via Cross-Harness Adaptation
